reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about forming a lubricious nanocrystalline Cr-rich oxide film on CoCrFeMnNi via controlled oxidation, but none of the cited evidence directly demonstrates this on the proposed alloy or treatment. E1 discusses tribo-oxidation forming protective nanocrystalline oxide glaze layers during high-temperature wear, supporting the general concept but not the specific pre-treatment. E2 describes native oxide removal leading to wear, not controlled oxidation benefits. E3 shows an oxide layer reducing friction on a different coating system (AlCrTiZrMo)N, not CoCrFe
premises: Controlled oxidation of CoCrFeMnNi at 400–600 °C forms a nanocrystalline Cr-rich oxide film
A nanocrystalline oxide film can act as a lubricious barrier reducing metal-metal contact
Such an oxide film reduces friction coefficient by ~25–35% and wear rate
The oxide film remains effective from room temperature to ~600 °C due to thermodynamic stability
Tribo-oxidation can form protective nanocrystalline oxide 'glaze layers' that provide solid lubrication
